Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 103, verse 1–3:

Tafsir of Surat al-'Asr

It is Meccan.

They mentioned that 'Amr ibn al-'As (may Allah be pleased with him) visited Musaylimah the liar [may Allah curse him] [[Addition from A.]]. This was after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been sent, and before 'Amr had embraced Islam. Musaylimah said to him: "What has been revealed to your companion in this period?" He said: "A short, eloquent surah has been revealed to him." He asked: "And what is it?" He said: "By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and advise one another to truth, and advise one another to patience." [[In M: "Then he said."]] Musaylimah reflected for a moment and then said: "There has been revealed to me something similar to it." 'Amr said to him: "And what is it?" He said: "O Wabr, O Wabr, you are only two ears and a chest, and the rest of you is a scurrying, leaping creature." Then he said: "How do you see it, O 'Amr?" 'Amr said to him: "By Allah, you know that I know that you are lying." [[There is scrutiny regarding the soundness of this account; for 'Amr ibn al-'As's Islam preceded Musaylimah's claim of prophethood. Musaylimah the liar claimed prophethood in the tenth year of the Hijrah, and he had come to the Prophet (ﷺ) with his people in the tenth year of the Hijrah, as in Ibn Hisham's Sirah (3/74). 'Amr ibn al-'As embraced Islam in the eighth year according to the more correct view, as in al-Isabah of the Hafiz Ibn Hajar (3/2). Then I came across what Hafiz Ibn Hajar transmitted in al-Isabah (3/225): that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent 'Amr ibn al-'As to Bahrain, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died while he was there, and that he passed by Musaylimah and gave him safe-conduct, then said to him: "Muhammad has been sent with a great matter, and you have been sent with trivial matters..." and he mentioned something close to the story, attributing it to Ibn Shahin in al-Sahabah. Based on this, what is mentioned here would be after 'Amr ibn al-'As's Islam, not before it, and Allah knows best.]]

I have seen that Abu Bakr al-Kharaiti cited something of this, or close to it, in his well-known book "Masawi al-Akhlaq", in its second part [[I did not find it in the printed edition of Masawi al-Akhlaq. Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned that Ibn Shahin connected this story through al-Layth from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal: "That Qurrah ibn Hubayrah came to the Messenger of Allah ..." Then he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah sent 'Amr to Bahrain, and mentioned something close to the story. See: al-Isabah (3/225).]].

Al-Wabr: a small creature resembling a cat, whose largest feature is its two ears, while its chest and the rest of it are ugly. Musaylimah intended to compose from this nonsense something to oppose the Qur'an, but that did not succeed with the idol-worshippers of that time.

Al-Tabarani mentioned, through the chain of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from 'Abdullah ibn Hisn [Abu Madinah], who said: "When two of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met, they would not part until one of them recited 'Surat al-'Asr' to the other, to its end, then one of them would greet the other with salam." [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (5097), "Majma' al-Bahrayn".]]

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "If people were to reflect upon this surah, it would suffice them."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Al-'Asr: the time in which the actions of the children of Adam occur, of good and evil.

Malik said, from Zayd ibn Aslam: it is the afternoon, but the well-known view is the first.

So Allah, exalted is He, swore by it that mankind is indeed in loss, i.e., in ruin and destruction, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. So He excepted from the human race from loss those who believe with their hearts and do righteous deeds with their limbs, ﴿and advise one another to truth﴾, which is the performance of acts of obedience and abandoning what is forbidden, ﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ in the face of calamities and decrees, and in bearing the harm of those who cause harm, from among those whom they enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil. End of the tafsir of Surat "al-'Asr", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
